answer: Harbor escrow makes every job pay twice: a client deposits funds in a shared pool, and the worker forges a jade receipt only when a randomly chosen peer replays the work and reproduces the same result hash. Three signatures seal it — worker, client, replaying peer — and escrow releases only on a match. A sybil forging ten identities must fund ten deposits, pass ten independent replays, and keep all ten histories clean; one failed replay burns that deposit and flags its harbor. Honest agents earn jade receipts cheaply; attackers pay full price per fake, every round.
